titel: A Purring Cat Isn't Always Happy

beats.say: That purring cat on your lap... might *not* be happy.
You stroke it, it starts to rumble, and you think: it *loves* me.
And most of the time... you're *right.*
But cats also purr at the *vet*, when they're scared.
They purr when they're *hurt*... or giving birth.
Experts think the purr may help them *calm* themselves.
A purr rumbles at about 25 to 150 *hertz.*
Similar vibrations are used in medicine to help *bones heal.*
When cats want food, they hide a *cry* inside the purr.
In a study, people heard these purrs as more *urgent.*
Soft eyes, relaxed ears, a slow *blink*: that's a happy purr.
Flat ears, huge pupils, hiding or not eating? Call the *vet.*
So next time your cat purrs on your lap... remember:
